result.title: Mechanistic Insights into LoRA: Layer Sparsity for Adaptive Fine-Tuning via Path Patching
result.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (Main Track). 31 pages, including appendices and the paper checklist
result.summary: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has emerged as the dominant paradigm for parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large language models. Standard all-layer LoRA applies adaptation throughout the transformer, despite heterogeneous contributions from its components. In this work, we conduct a systematic mechanistic interpretability analysis to understand how LoRA affects model internals. We observe that LoRA's adaptation effect is highly non-uniform, with significant component-wise and layer-wise sparsity. Most critically, we find that important layers are highly task-dependent, with limited overlap across tasks. Motivated by these insights, we propose Adaptive-LoRA, a calibration-driven method that automatically identifies task-specific layers via frozen-base zero-ablation, enabling efficient layer selection without exhaustive search. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-1.5B across 11 diverse reasoning tasks demonstrate that Adaptive-LoRA outperforms full-layer LoRA while using only 30% of layers, achieving a $3.5\times$ reduction in adapter parameters. This work bridges mechanistic interpretability and practical efficiency, providing both fundamental insights and a principled approach for adaptive fine-tuning.

AI.brief_summary: 用 path patching 与冻结基座零消融系统分析 LoRA 在 transformer 内部的作用，发现其效果在组件与层间高度稀疏、且重要层强依赖具体任务，据此提出只选取约 30% 层的 Adaptive-LoRA。
AI.relevance_reason: 其因果干预式的层贡献定位（path patching、zero-ablation）与自动选层流程，可供核查 LVR 中适配器应注入哪些层、以及 latent 推理状态的贡献如何归因；但属纯文本设定，迁移到视觉推理需验证。
